schema_documentation:
Identical 3-key schema and identical 18 metadata sub-keys to the other two `common_corpus` folders: `text` (str, 100%), `id` (str, 100%, = `metadata.url`), `metadata` (dict, 100%) with `name`(=common_corpus), `collection`, `open_type`, `license`, `date` (float 100% in stats, 1521–2023), `title`, `creator`, `language`(=`und`), `language_type`(=Spoken), `language_score`, `language_script`(=Grek), `word_count`, `token_count`, `url`, `dataset`, `file_path`, `shard_id`, `__index_level_0__`.

Measured `collection` over 1,357 records: Greek-PD 93.1%, Eurovoc 2.9%, Latin-PD 2.0%, German-PD 0.7%, French-Science-Pile 0.3%, Eurlex 0.3%, Marianne-Europe 0.2%, then Spanish-Science-Pile / Italian-PD / WTO / French Open Data / Open-Science-Pile / US-PD-Newspapers ≤0.1% each. README claimed Greek-PD 93.6% — verified.

The giveaway is `metadata.title`/`creator`, which are Latin/French/Italian: 'R.mi P.F. Antonij a Spiritu Sancto … Directorium mysticum' (1697), 'Nouissimus Collegij Complutensis … Artium cursus' (1676), 'Theologia moralis … Thomae Tamburini' (1755), 'Corps de philosophie … par M. Scipion Du Pleix' (1626).
semantic_meaning: Not Greek: 16th–18th-century Latin/French/Italian/Spanish books OCR'd through a Greek-glyph character map, producing unreadable pseudo-Greek.
split_group_rule: Hash originating source identity; dictionary by normalized lemma; recipes by normalized title; sentiment by complete normalized review; AMNA by validated article ID; Photodentro by validated learning-object ID. Global duplicate components must share a split.
validation_rules: Rebuild full user prompt and answer from preserved evidence
Independent Greek grammar/naturalness review remains mandatory
